chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said:
Is'haq ibn Umar bequeathed at the time of his death regarding his slave-girl singers that we should sell them and carry their price to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him).

Ibrahim said: So I sold the slave-girls for three hundred thousand dirhams and carried the price to him. I said to him: Indeed, a mawla of yours, called Is'haq ibn Umar, has bequeathed at the time of his death the selling of his slave-girl singers and carrying the price to you. I have sold them, and this price is three hundred thousand dirhams.

He (peace be upon him) said: I have no need for it. Indeed, this is ill-gotten gain (suh't). Teaching them is disbelief (kufr), and listening to them is hypocrisy (nifaq), and their price is ill-gotten gain (suh't).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the earnings of female singers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad conveys the verdict of Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) regarding the wealth derived from female singers, declaring it *suh't* (ill-gotten gain). The Imam provides a tripartite theological classification: teaching them constitutes *kufr* (disbelief), listening to them is *nifaq* (hypocrisy), and their earnings are *suh't*, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual impurity of their art and its impact on the listener's faith. This ruling underscores the broader principle that the source of income is intrinsically linked to the nature of the activity itself.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from one of his companions, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, form Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad who said,
‘Is’haq Bin Umar bequeathed at the time of his death with the selling of his slave girl singers that we should sell them and carry their price over to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>.

Ibrahim (the narrator) said, ‘So I sold the slave girls for three hundred thousand Dirhams, and carried the price to him<sup>asws</sup>, so I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘One in your<sup>asws</sup> Wilayah, called Is’haq Bin Umar has bequeathed at the time of his death for the selling of his singer slave girls and deliver the price over to you<sup>asws</sup>, and I have sold them, and this is the price, three hundred thousand Dirhams’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no need for me<sup>asws</sup> with regards to it. This is an ill-gotten gain, teaching them is disbelief, and listening from them is hypocrisy, and their price is an ill-gotten gain’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from certain persons of his people from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il from Ibrahim ibn abu al-Balad who has said the following:
“Ishaq ibn ‘Umar made a will about his singer slave-girls at the time when he was about to die that said, ‘They must be sold and funds from their sale delivered to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam.

Ibrahim has said, ‘I sold the slave-girls for three hundred thousand dirham and took it to him (the Imam) and said, ‘One of your followers, called Ishaq ibn ‘Umar has made a will at the time he was about to die to sell his singer slave-girls and take the funds from their sale to you. I have sold them and this is the three hundred thousand dirham from the sale.
He (the Imam) said, ‘I do not need them. It is Suht (filthy), teaching them is disbelief, listening to them is hypocrisy and funds from their sale are Suht (filthy) unlawful.’”
